Fitted to the facelift W223 S-Class, W167 GLE, and X167 GLS, reconditioned OM656 engines typically start from £3,200 , serving as the definitive premium diesel for modern flagship and executive chassis.

costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz OM656.950 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an OM656 engine typically takes 10-14 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the condition of the AdBlue dosing module, the EGR cooler, and the 48V Integrated Starter Generator (ISG). Because the OM656.950 is a highly complex modern common-rail unit, recon specialists will typically verify the ISG health, update all software maps to the latest Euro 6e calibration, and replace the EGR cooler as standard. For a full breakdown of market rates, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM656.950 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: AdBlue System Faults
items.whatHappens: The AdBlue dosing module, heater, or NOx sensors can fail, leading to warning lights, restricted performance (limp mode), and eventually a no-start condition if the tank is depleted and the system is locked out by the ECU.
items.repairVsReplace: Often resolved by replacing the dosing module or NOx sensor, which is a standard repair. If the tank heater or pump has failed, a full tank assembly replacement may be required.

items.title: EGR Cooler Leaks
items.whatHappens: The internal matrix of the EGR cooler can crack, allowing coolant to mix with exhaust gases or enter the intake manifold. This leads to unexplained coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust, and potential hydrolock if severe.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR cooler replacement is a standard repair. If caught early, it prevents catastrophic internal engine damage.

items.title: Mild-Hybrid (ISG) Integration Issues
items.whatHappens: The Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) is a complex 48V component. While generally reliable, software glitches or electrical faults can cause start-stop malfunctions, reduced EQ Boost assistance, or warning lights.
items.repairVsReplace: Most ISG issues are resolved via software updates or replacing the 48V auxiliary battery. Full ISG replacement is rare but costly if the unit itself fails.

failures.goodYearsLine: The OM656.950 is the latest and most refined revision of the OM656 family, building on an already highly robust foundation. Units maintained with strict AdBlue top-ups and regular oil changes routinely exceed 150,000 miles without major internal issues .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes-Benz OM656.950
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, near the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. The OM656.950 is the updated, higher-output variant of the OM656 family. It is sometimes confused with the earlier OM656.930/940 (which features different output tuning and earlier Euro 6d emissions hardware) or the smaller 2.0L inline-4 OM654. Fitting the wrong revision or assuming interchangeability matters significantly: the OM656.950 features specific updated 48V ISG calibration, revised turbo plumbing, and Euro 6e ECU mapping that will not function correctly if swapped with an earlier OM656 or an OM654 without extensive and costly modification.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM656.950 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM656.950 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and documented proof that the AdBlue system, EGR cooler, and 48V ISG are in good working order. Given the complexity of modern hybrid emissions systems, buying a used unit with unknown history is a significant financial risk.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM656 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by verifying the AdBlue dosing module, replacing the EGR cooler, and refreshing all critical seals, giving the engine a fresh lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM656 engine rebuild is justified for high-mileage W223 S-Class or W167 GLE hosts where maximum longevity and originality are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM656 engine is installed by specialists familiar with modern Mercedes CDI and mild-hybrid systems, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the OM656.950 is typically found in modern W223, W167, and X167 vehicles valued between £40,000 and £120,000+, a full replacement is highly financially viable and comfortably within the host vehicle's value . Replacement cost rarely exceeds the scrap threshold for these modern flagship chassis, making a reconditioned unit a highly sensible investment.

items.question: How much does a Mercedes OM656.950 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes OM656.950 engine typically costs between £3,200 and £5,500 for supply only . Fitted costs generally range from £3,850 to £6,410 depending on the specialist, while used units can be found from £1,800 but carry higher risk due to the complexity of the modern emissions and hybrid systems. items.question: What is the most common failure on the OM656.950 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are AdBlue system faults, EGR cooler leaks, and occasional mild-hybrid (ISG) integration issues. AdBlue dosing module or NOx sensor failures trigger limp mode, while EGR cooler cracks can lead to unexplained coolant loss and white smoke from the exhaust. items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned OM656.950 engine?
